version.changelog:
Initial release — A comprehensive, end-to-end management system for the computer science PhD research lifecycle.

- Supports literature surveys with multi-source search (arXiv, DBLP, ACM, IEEE) and technical thread identification.
- Tracks advisor communications and meeting action items for systematic research direction alignment.
- Enables paper writing with version control and support for iterative revision cycles (6–8 rounds).
- Provides robust experiment design, including comparison and ablation studies with automated logging.
- Includes mathematical consistency validation and full scientific traceability to meet audit and publication standards.
- Delivers standardized, compliant output directories for reproducible, well-documented academic workflows.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: phd-research-companion
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle defines a comprehensive end-to-end workflow for PhD research management, covering literature surveys, advisor communication, and paper iteration. While the SKILL.md file describes high-privilege operations such as multi-source network searches (arXiv, IEEE, etc.), local file system organization, and Git-based version control, these capabilities are strictly aligned with the stated academic purpose. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, credential theft, or malicious prompt injection; the 'Scientific Traceability' system is designed for local audit compliance rather than unauthorized data removal. The bundle contains no actual executable code, relying instead on the agent to follow the structured markdown instructions.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only PhD workflow guide (no installs or credentials), which is broadly coherent with its description, but the SKILL.md contains detected unicode control characters (a common prompt-injection technique) and the file is from an unknown source — inspect before allowing it to run or have the agent act autonomously.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (end-to-end PhD research companion) matches the SKILL.md content: guidance for literature survey, experiment logging, advisor meeting tracking, and traceability. It does not request credentials or install anything, which is plausible for a purely instructional skill. One mismatch to note: it advertises automated multi-source literature review (arXiv/DBLP/ACM/IEEE). Automation of these sources may require scraping or API access; the skill does not declare APIs, tokens, or tools for that purpose, so the implementation approach is unspecified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is long and prescriptive about creating directories and storing sensitive items (meeting attendee lists, advisor-signed PDFs, detailed logs). The pre-scan flagged unicode-control-chars inside the SKILL.md, which is a known sign of hidden/obfuscated prompt-injection that can change how an agent interprets instructions or hide malicious directives. Because this file is the runtime instruction set and originates from an unknown source, the presence of control characters is concerning and warrants manual inspection of the raw SKILL.md for hidden content or altered directives. Also check for any steps that instruct the agent to read arbitrary local files or environment variables — none are declared, but hidden text could add such steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files — the skill is instruction-only. That reduces risk because nothing will be written to disk or auto-installed by the skill itself.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. For the stated purposes this is reasonable (it's largely a procedural/organizational workflow). Be cautious if later prompts or instructions ask the user to paste credentials, API keys, or other secrets — those would be out of band and not declared here.

llm.guidance: This skill is instruction-only and broadly matches its stated purpose, but the SKILL.md comes from an unknown source and contains unicode control characters (a red flag for hidden prompt-injection). Before installing or enabling autonomous use: (1) open the raw SKILL.md in a text editor that can display invisible/control characters and review it line-by-line for unexpected instructions or requests to access files/credentials; (2) confirm the referenced GitHub repo and maintainer contact independently (the documentation_url points to a repo but source is unknown); (3) do not paste secrets or API keys into prompts from this skill; (4) if you plan to allow autonomous invocation, first run the skill in a restricted/sandboxed environment and monitor network and filesystem activity; (5) prefer skills with a verifiable source or included code so you can audit behavior — if you cannot verify the content of SKILL.md, treat it as untrusted.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Detected unicode control characters inside SKILL.md. This is not expected for a benign instructional document and is a common method to obfuscate or inject hidden directives that change how an agent parses or follows instructions. Manual review of the raw file (showing invisible characters) is recommended before running.
